issues.description: _BufferingHandler buffer is unbounded with no size cap or drop policy.
issues.detail: buffer is a plain list that grows without limit between _start_log_buffering and flush/cleanup. A slow crash or chatty DEBUG library can balloon memory before the worker notices. Use a bounded deque(maxlen=N) or ring buffer with an explicit drop policy enforced in emit().

issues.description: OTLP handler discovered by isinstance scan over root logger handlers instead of held by reference.
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer iterates logging.getLogger().handlers to find the LoggingHandler that _setup_cloud_tracer installed. Setup knows exactly which handler it added; store and pass that reference. The scan couples JobContext to telemetry internals, leaks abstraction, and is fragile if other LoggingHandlers exist.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry mutates global root logger handlers, silently dropping handlers it does not own.
issues.detail: It strips every LoggingHandler from the root logger before force_flush, collateral-damaging any non-OTLP LoggingHandler a user installed. The narrow fix for re-entrant emit during flush is to detach only the handler this module installed, by reference. Document the frame or narrow the scope.

issues.description: init_recording overloaded: _on_cleanup synthesizes RecordingOptions to opportunistically flush crash logs.
issues.detail: init_recording's clean precondition (not initialized AND cloud URL) and single postcondition are now reused from cleanup with audio/traces/transcript=False just to push logs. Split into init_recording and a dedicated _ensure_crash_log_pipeline / teardown call so contracts and intent stay visible.

issues.description: Four parallel JobContext lifecycle methods should collapse into a single LogBuffer object.
issues.detail: _start_log_buffering, _stop_log_buffering, _flush_early_log_buffer, and the _on_cleanup branch all manage one handler with a None-dance on _early_log_handler. A small LogBuffer owning attach/detach/replay with a bounded deque would let the buffer be a value, the sink a policy, and the algorithm disappear.

issues.description: Unrelated makefile, worker.py, and test changes bundled into the crash-log PR.
issues.detail: Disabling pytest -n auto, dropping test_plugin_google_stt, the test_ipc retry-batch edit, and the worker.py reorder registering _pending_assignments before queuing availability_resp are separate stories. The worker fix is load-bearing and deserves a comment; the test-infra changes deserve their own PR so regressions are attributable and revertable.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the crash-log upload intent is right but the implementation leaks abstractions and lacks invariants. Three structural defects recur across all reviewers: an unbounded log buffer, OTLP handler discovery via isinstance scan over the root logger, and _shutdown_telemetry mutating global handler state it does not own. Two reviewers also flag that init_recording has been overloaded by _on_cleanup synthesizing RecordingOptions, and that four JobContext lifecycle methods should collapse into a single LogBuffer value owning a bounded deque and its handler reference. Finally, the makefile, worker.py reorder, and test changes are unrelated and should travel as separate PRs.
